concept.name: Staking
concept.definition: Staking is the act of depositing a network's native token to activate validator software that secures a proof-of-stake chain — proposing and attesting to blocks — in exchange for protocol rewards, with penalties (slashing) for misbehavior or downtime.
concept.intuition: Staking is posting a performance bond to become part-time infrastructure: do the work honestly and you earn a yield on your deposit; cheat or sleep and part of the deposit burns.
concept.mechanics: On Ethereum, solo staking requires 32 ETH and running execution, consensus and validator clients; rewards accrue for attestations, block proposals and sync duties, while offline validators leak small penalties and equivocating validators are slashed and ejected. Alternatives with lower barriers include pooled staking, staking-as-a-service, liquid staking and exchange staking, each adding its own trust assumptions.
concept.failure_modes: Slashing (including correlated mass slashing) and inactivity penalties reduce stake; custodial and pooled staking concentrate funds and validators, creating central points of failure; staking yields are diluted as more of the supply stakes (issuance per validator falls with total stake).
concept.misconceptions: Staking is not a risk-free interest account — rewards pay for active duties and capital at risk, and third-party staking adds counterparty and smart contract risk. The APR is not fixed: it falls as total stake rises and varies with network activity (tips, MEV).
concept.example: A solo staker with 32 ETH earns roughly 3-4% APR from consensus rewards plus priority fees and MEV when proposing blocks; a validator offline for days loses small daily penalties, while double-signing can cost 1+ ETH and forced exit.
